I am 70 now. I went to primary school only, so I read a little but not much. I farm 24 mu — that is a lot for just me and my wife. My son works in the city. I hire a little help at harvest and for spraying.

I do wheat and maize like everyone in Quzhou. Wheat goes in October, maize in June right after wheat. This rotation I have done for 40 years. The county agriculture station sometimes comes, and the fertilizer seller in town tells me what is new, but I mostly do what worked last year.

Last year wheat gave me about 500 kg per mu, maize about 600 kg per mu. Not bad. I do not want less this year.

For wheat: I buy compound fertilizer 15-15-15, two bags per mu as base before planting. That is 100 jin, so 50 kg — gives me about 7.5 kg N, 7.5 P, 7.5 K each mu. Then in spring at jointing I topdress urea, one bag (50 jin, 25 kg) per 2 mu — so about 12 kg urea per mu, that is 5-6 kg N more. Total N around 13-14 kg per mu. I use improved wheat seed from the station, Jimai type, everyone around here uses it. I water the wheat — winter water before freeze, then jointing water, then grain-filling water. Three times with my well. I spray herbicide once in spring for weeds, and one time against aphids and rust in April. Two sprays. Plough after maize harvest because wheat needs loose soil.

For maize: I plant right after wheat harvest, no-till with the seeder, that saves time and diesel. Hybrid maize seed — Zhengdan or Xianyu type, whatever the dealer has good price. I put one bag compound 15-15-15 at sowing, 50 jin per mu, then topdress urea at big trumpet stage, about 20 kg urea per mu (roughly 9 kg N). So maize gets maybe 15 kg N per mu total. Maize needs water in July if no rain — usually one or two irrigations from the well. Spray once for corn borer, maybe twice if worms are bad.

I do not want to change too much. Fertilizer price went up, but skipping costs more in yield. I would rather use a little extra than short the crop.
